subject: Horizon Health RFP - Hybrid concurrency & time-of-day pricing questions
messages:
From: Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on commercial appendix - concurrency vs token tiers

Marcus,

Thanks for the commercial appendix you submitted with the RFP. Our finance and infra teams want clarity on two specific items before we proceed to the technical evaluation: 1) how a hybrid "reserved concurrency" commitment interacts with per-token overage billing (do we get per-token discounts when reserved concurrency is active?), and 2) whether you support time-of-day or schedule-based pricing (we have peak windows for clinical workflows).

We'd appreciate an example invoice for a month where we use reserved concurrency 24/7 vs a month where we have large daytime spikes but low overnight usage. Also, please call out any minimum monthly commitment floors and the mechanics of true-ups.

Can you send a short commercial write-up (bullets + sample calc) and any supporting spreadsheet?

Best,
Danielle
Director, Procurement
Horizon Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on commercial appendix - concurrency vs token tiers

Danielle — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short commercial summary and a sample invoice workbook (Horizon-RFP-Commercial-Appendix.xlsx). Key points up-front: 

- Hybrid model summary: Reserved Concurrency Units (RCUs) + per-token billing. RCUs reserve serving capacity for predictable latency; RCUs are billed as a monthly commitment (USD/month) and include a per-token consumption allowance (tokens included = RCUs * 2M tokens/month baseline).
- When RCUs are active, per-token usage beyond the included allowance is billed at the "committed overage" rate (lower than on-demand), not the on-demand public rate. That is, having RCUs gives you a discounted overage band.
- Time-of-day pricing: we offer a schedule-based multiplier for workloads with predictable diurnal patterns. Example: daytime multiplier 1.0 (standard), off-peak multiplier 0.75 applied to per-token charge when traffic falls within customer-defined windows. Multipliers do not apply to the RCU monthly fee.
- Minimums & true-up: Minimum monthly commitment floor = 3 RCUs for Enterprise. True-up on a trailing-quarter basis: if your trailing 90-day aggregate consumption exceeds committed tokens by >15%, additional tokens are invoiced at the committed overage rate; if underutilized >25% we offer one-time carry-forward credit up to the committed allowance.

Sample month calc (in workbook):
- Scenario A (steady 24/7): 3 RCUs committed, includes 6M tokens/month. Usage = 5.8M tokens -> no overage, RCU bill only.
- Scenario B (day spike): 3 RCUs committed, includes 6M tokens. Usage = 9.2M tokens (7.0M daytime, 2.2M off-peak). Daytime billed at committed overage rate for tokens beyond included, off-peak billed at 0.75 multiplier on per-token rate for tokens beyond included. Total invoice = RCU monthly fee + committed overage for daytime + off-peak discounted overage.

I've kept the workbook calculations explicit (line items for RCU fee, included tokens, committed overage band, off-peak multiplier). Karthik and Laura — tagging you for any commercial guardrails or edits before I send a formal pricing schedule and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Horizon Health RFP - commercial write-up (review + ask)

Team — forwarding Horizon's clarifying Qs. Short internal note: Horizon needs a hybrid commit that reduces per-token overage and supports time-of-day discounts. Their security and procurement teams will require a one-year committed term with quarterly true-up.

My proposal (draft):
- Year 1: 3 RCUs committed. Base RCU monthly fee = $24,000 per RCU (examples in pricebook). Included tokens = 2M tokens per RCU per month (6M total). Committed overage = $0.0009 per token up to 3x included allowance, after which on-demand public rate applies.
- Off-peak multiplier = 0.75 applied to committed overage rate for hours between 22:00-06:00 local time (customer-configurable).
- First-year customer intro discount: 12% off RCU fee for the first 6 months if signed by EOM.
- Billing & true-up: monthly invoicing; trailing-quarter true-up with adjustment invoice and payment terms Net30.

Ask: Karthik — are the per-RCU list price and overage breakpoint reasonable? Laura — any procurement flags (minimum term, credits, carry-forward?) I expect they'll push for a larger carry-forward cap and possibly a longer introductory discount.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Horizon Health RFP - commercial write-up (review + ask)

Marcus — numbers look directionally fine. A few guardrails and recommended edits: 

- Pricebook tweak: reduce per-RCU listed fee to $22,500 for health-care vertical deals with a 12-month commit; keep the included token assumption at 2M/RCU. This gives more headroom for discounting while preserving margin.
- Overage bands: change committed overage band to $0.00085 per token for up to 4x included allowance, thereafter apply on-demand at $0.0018. This provides Horizon a predictable mid-band.
- Intro discount: keep 12% for 6 months but move approval to Sales Leader sign-off for anything deeper.
- Carry-forward: increase carry-forward credit to up to 50% of unused included tokens per quarter (one-time only) instead of 25%.
- Legal: Laura, note that true-up frequency quarterly is OK; procurement may ask to move to annual true-up — prefer to keep quarterly to align billing accuracy.

If these adjustments look good I recommend returning to Horizon with a single-sheet commercial summary and a DocuSign MSA link.

Karthik
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Marcus — thank you for the detailed write-up and the sample workbook. A few clarifying Qs before I take this to budget committee: 

1) If we scale to 9 RCUs in year 2, do the included tokens scale linearly? Are there step discounts for larger multi-RCU commitments?
2) For months with bursting beyond 4x included allowance, can you provide a cap or emergency burst credit to prevent runaway invoices?
3) Please attach a one-page example invoice for Scenario B showing line items and the calculation for off-peak multiplier; the workbook is great but leadership wants a one-pager.

If you can incorporate Karthik's edited rates into the one-pager and include an explicit line for the carry-forward credit mechanics, we can move to internal sign-off next week.

Best,
Danielle
Director, Procurement
Horizon Health
